venues.note: A long-running hillside seafood house above Ao Nang with a sweeping sunset view over the bay, the town's landmark table.
credentials: Ao Nang's best-known destination seafood restaurant, a long-established local landmark with panoramic bay views

venues.name: Carnivore Steak & Grill
venues.note: Ao Nang's serious steakhouse, proper cuts and a cellar for the member who wants beef done well after days of seafood.
credentials: Ao Nang's leading established steakhouse, a long-standing fixture on the town's dining strip

venues.name: Railay Peninsula, arriving only by longtail boat
venues.note: A tiny peninsula cut off from the mainland by sheer limestone walls, so there are no roads in, you step off a longtail boat straight onto the sand. That severance is the whole point: no cars, no through-traffic, just four beaches, climbers on the cliffs and the karsts glowing at dusk. The obvious base for a honeymoon or a family that wants Krabi's drama without Phuket's noise.

venues.name: Railay West Beach
venues.note: The postcard beach, a soft white crescent framed by towering karsts, where the longtails pull in and the sun sets straight down the water. It is where Rayavadee and the smart resorts sit, and where you gather at dusk with a drink to watch the cliffs turn amber. Calm, swimmable and the social heart of the peninsula.

venues.name: Railay East Beach & the mangrove boardwalk
venues.note: The quieter, mangrove-fringed side of the peninsula, muddy at low tide and not for swimming, but this is where the boats to Ao Nang and Krabi Town dock and where the cheaper bars and climbing shops cluster. A five-minute walk on the flat path links it to Railay West, so you can stay on the pretty side and pass through here to move around.

venues.name: Phra Nang Cave Beach (Hat Tham Phra Nang)
venues.note: Regularly rated one of the most beautiful beaches on earth, a short walk from Railay East past the Rayavadee grounds delivers you to a jewel of white sand tucked under a colossal overhang, with karst islets offshore and water the colour of glass. Longtails sell fresh fruit and cold beer off the water. Arrive early; by midday the day-trip boats crowd in.

venues.name: Princess Cave (Tham Phra Nang Nok) & the fertility shrine
venues.note: At the end of Phra Nang beach, a cave holds a shrine to a sea princess where local fishermen leave carved wooden phalluses as offerings for a good catch and fertility, an unmissable, slightly startling piece of living folklore. It takes two minutes to see and gives the beach its name and its spirit.

venues.name: The Princess Lagoon (Sa Phra Nang) hike
venues.note: A hidden emerald pool sunk deep inside the karst, reached only by a genuinely demanding scramble down ropes and mud from the viewpoint trail, around 45 minutes of rock-clinging descent to a still lagoon walled by cliffs. Strictly for the fit and sure-footed, but the reward is a secret world almost no day-tripper reaches.

venues.name: Railay Viewpoint
venues.note: A short but steep, rope-assisted climb off the East–Phra Nang trail opens onto the definitive photograph of Railay: both beaches, the whole peninsula and the Andaman laid out below. Ten to twenty sweaty minutes up; wear proper shoes and go at high tide for the full effect.

venues.name: Rock climbing on the Railay & Ton Sai crags
venues.note: Railay is one of the world's great climbing destinations, hundreds of bolted routes on sea-cliff limestone, from beginner walls above Railay East to overhanging test-pieces at Ton Sai. Reputable schools run half-day introductions with guides and gear, so a first-timer or a teenager can top out over the sea by lunch. Deep-water soloing off a boat is the adrenaline upgrade.

venues.name: Ton Sai Beach
venues.note: The rugged, bohemian neighbour of Railay, a rocky-at-low-tide bay backed by jungle and the climbing crowd, reached by a scramble over the headland or a short longtail hop. Rawer and cheaper than Railay proper; worth a wander for the climber-café atmosphere and the sense of Railay before the resorts.

venues.name: Ao Nang, the mainland base and beach town
venues.note: The busy beach town on the mainland that most trips run from: the pier for every island tour, a long promenade of restaurants (including reliable Indian and clearly-labelled vegetarian kitchens), dive shops and hotels. Not the prettiest beach in Krabi, but the logistics hub, the longtails to Railay leave from here, and it is where a family stocks up between excursions.

venues.name: Nopparat Thara Beach & the Mu Ko Phi Phi–Nopparat Thara National Park
venues.note: A long, quiet, casuarina-shaded beach just west of Ao Nang that most visitors overlook, at low tide a sandbar links out to a small island. It is the mainland gateway of the marine national park that also covers Phi Phi, and a calmer alternative to the Ao Nang strip for a slow local morning.

venues.name: The Four Islands day trip
venues.note: Krabi's signature outing, Phra Nang Cave Beach, Chicken Island, Tup Island and Poda Island in one loop of white sand, snorkelling and karst scenery. Charter a private longtail or speedboat and time it around the tide so you have the beaches before the crowds; the classic honeymoon and multi-gen day on the water.

venues.name: The Tup Island sandbar (Koh Tup / Koh Mor)
venues.note: At low tide a ribbon of white sand rises from the sea to link three islands, and you can walk from one to another across the ocean floor, Krabi's most photographed natural trick and a genuine delight for children. It appears only for a few hours a day, so a good boatman plans the whole trip around the tide table.

venues.name: Poda Island (Koh Poda)
venues.note: A near-perfect little island of powder sand and clear shallows with a lone karst pinnacle rising offshore, the quintessential Krabi beach for swimming, sunbathing and a picnic lunch. Charter your own boat to have it before the tour fleet arrives.

venues.name: The Hong Islands (Mu Ko Hong) & the hidden lagoon
venues.note: 'Hong' means 'room', and the star island hides an enclosed emerald lagoon reached through a narrow gap in the cliffs, opening into a walled world of still turquoise water. Often quieter and arguably lovelier than Phi Phi; the private-longtail version, paddling in by kayak, is one of Krabi's most romantic mornings.

venues.name: Sea-kayaking the Hong lagoon
venues.note: The Hong lagoon is fully enclosed and sheltered, so even a complete novice can paddle in through the rock gate and drift under 100-metre cliffs reflected in glassy water. A gentle, photogenic activity that suits couples, grandparents and children alike, the calm counterpoint to the Ao Thalane mangroves.

venues.name: The Phi Phi Islands day trip
venues.note: The famous day out from Ao Nang or Railay, Phi Phi Leh's soaring cliffs and lagoons, the snorkelling, Monkey Beach and lunch on Phi Phi Don. Go by private speedboat at sunrise to reach Maya Bay and Pileh before the fleet; the difference between a magical morning and a floating traffic jam is entirely about timing.

venues.name: Maya Bay, 'The Beach'
venues.note: The cove made world-famous by the Leonardo DiCaprio film, a flawless bowl of white sand walled by cliffs, reopened under strict rules after years of recovery, with no swimming at the beach and a boardwalk approach from the back of the island. Note the seasonal closure: the bay shuts to visitors every 1 August–30 September (2026 included) to let the reef rest. First boat in, before 9am, is the only way to have it feel wild.

venues.name: Pileh Lagoon
venues.note: A long, narrow inlet almost slicing Phi Phi Leh in two, walled by 100-metre cliffs with unreal turquoise water and a soft white sand bottom, no coral, so it is safe to float and swim freely. Often the highlight of the whole Phi Phi day; arrive early and it can feel like a private cathedral of rock.

venues.name: Viking Cave (Tham Phaya Nak)
venues.note: A vast sea cave named for ancient wall paintings that resemble longships, and still worked by sea-gypsy collectors of prized swiftlet nests. The cave itself is closed to landings, so boats slow to let you look from the water, a brief but atmospheric stop on the Phi Phi loop.

venues.name: Bamboo Island (Koh Phai)
venues.note: A low, sandy island north of Phi Phi Don ringed by a wide curve of white beach and shallow reef in two to four metres of water, the best snorkelling stop of the Phi Phi day and a lovely place to simply lie on the sand. Part of the national park, so a fee applies and it can close in low season.

venues.name: Koh Lanta, the slow island
venues.note: A long, laid-back island south of Krabi reached by car ferry or road bridges, strung with a dozen quieter beaches that grow emptier the further south you drive. This is where you go to decompress after the island tours, think honeymoon stillness, sunset dinners and a pace that Ao Nang no longer has.

venues.name: Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya)
venues.note: A photogenic old Chinese-Thai fishing village of stilted wooden shophouses over the water on Lanta's east coast, seafood restaurants on the piers, small galleries and craft shops, and a gentle, unhurried afternoon of strolling. The most characterful town on the island and a window into its trading past.

venues.name: Kantiang Bay
venues.note: A gorgeous horseshoe of sand near Lanta's southern end, cradled by jungle-clad cliffs and home to the island's most upmarket resort, the drive over the hills to reach it is half the pleasure. One of the loveliest and least crowded beaches in the whole Krabi region for a couple seeking quiet.

venues.name: Mu Ko Lanta National Park & the lighthouse (Laem Tanod)
venues.note: At Lanta's southern tip, a national park headland crowned by a small lighthouse gives a sweeping panorama of sea, cliffs and islands, with a short jungle nature trail where you may meet resident monkeys. The end-of-the-island reward after a scenic coastal drive past Kantiang and Bamboo bays.

venues.name: Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea), the 1,237-step climb
venues.note: A working meditation temple wrapped around a cave where a monk once saw tigers, with a brutally steep staircase of over 1,200 steps rising 280-odd metres to a golden Buddha and a 360-degree view across Krabi to the Andaman. A serious 40–60 minute climb in the heat, best at dawn; profoundly worth it for the fit. Free to enter.

venues.name: The Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot)
venues.note: A natural spring-fed pool of impossibly clear, milky-jade water in the rainforest of the Khao Phra Bang Khram sanctuary, warm, swimmable and ringed by jungle, reached by an easy boardwalk. About an hour from Ao Nang and usually paired with the Blue Pool; go early before the tour buses. Small entry fee.

venues.name: The Blue Pool (Sa Nam Phut)
venues.note: A short jungle walk beyond the Emerald Pool, this geothermal spring glows an almost electric sapphire when the light hits, deep, hot and not for swimming, but mesmerising to stand over. Opens later than the Emerald Pool (from 10am); the two together make the definitive Krabi rainforest half-day.

venues.name: The natural hot springs (Nam Tok Ron)
venues.note: A cascade of smooth stone pools where warm mineral water tumbles down the rock into a cool stream, you soak in a natural jacuzzi in the jungle and then dip in the cold pool below. Usually combined with the Emerald and Blue Pools into one restorative inland day; soothing for grandparents and children alike.

venues.name: Than Bok Khorani National Park
venues.note: An easily-missed mainland park north of Krabi where an emerald pool fed by a limestone spring spreads through a small botanical forest of orchids, gingers and wild gardenias, swimmable, serene and blissfully untouristed. A gentle nature stop and the launch point for the Bor Thor cave-and-mangrove kayaking.

venues.name: Khao Khanab Nam, the twin karst cliffs
venues.note: The two limestone towers that guard the mouth of the Krabi River are the emblem of the town, a fifteen-minute longtail ride upstream from the pier. Land to explore the caves at their base, where stalactites and traces of prehistoric human habitation have been found. A short, evocative outing that doubles as a river cruise past the mangroves.

venues.name: Sea-kayaking the Ao Thalane mangroves
venues.note: Paddle silent channels through cathedral-like limestone canyons and mangrove tunnels, gliding past macaques, mudskippers, kingfishers and the occasional monkey trying to hitch a ride. Gentle enough for the whole family and, at the right tide, one of the most atmospheric wildlife experiences in Krabi, the wild counterpart to the polished Hong lagoon.

venues.name: Kayaking Klong Root (Crystal Lagoon)
venues.note: A freshwater lagoon fed by an underground spring, so clear you can watch fish and submerged trees beneath the kayak as you paddle through a green, silent, Jurassic-feeling jungle. Quieter and more surreal than the sea kayaking; a lovely, low-effort morning for couples and families who want stillness.

venues.name: Tha Pom Khlong Song Nam, the 'two-water canal'
venues.note: A short boardwalk trail follows a crystal stream where fresh spring water meets the Andaman's saltwater, turning the shallows a vivid emerald that shifts with the tide, you can cool off in the clear pool where the two waters mix. A quiet, easy nature walk near Ao Nang that most visitors never find.

venues.name: Susan Hoi, the Fossil Shell Beach
venues.note: One of only a handful of shell-fossil beaches on earth: a 200-metre shelf of grey rock made entirely of freshwater snail shells fused into stone over tens of millions of years, cracking off in great slabs at the sea's edge. A genuinely rare geological curiosity, quick to see and fascinating for children and curious travellers.

venues.name: Krabi Town Walking Street night market
venues.note: On weekend evenings the old town's Maharat Soi 8 fills with food stalls, a live stage and lantern-lit lanes, grilled seafood, mango sticky rice, southern curries and plenty of clearly-marked vegetarian and fruit stalls. The most authentic, unpolished evening in the area and an easy, atmospheric night out away from the resort strip.

venues.name: Sunset dinner on Phra Nang beach at Rayavadee
venues.note: Rayavadee's celebrated 'The Grotto' sets tables inside a limestone cave right on Phra Nang beach, cocktails and dinner under the karst as the sun drops, arguably the single most romantic table in Krabi. A private-yacht or longtail transfer turns dinner into an occasion for a honeymoon or anniversary.

venues.name: Private-yacht island-hopping & sunset sailing
venues.note: Charter a private yacht or luxury catamaran to trace the Four Islands, Hong and Phi Phi archipelagos at your own pace, with a chef, a swim platform and the karsts to yourselves at golden hour. The definitive way for an UHNI family to see Krabi, no crowds, your own tide plan, and a sundowner sail back into the cliffs.

venues.name: Private longtail charter for the day
venues.note: The most authentic, and surprisingly attainable, luxury here is your own long-tail boat and boatman for the day, so you land on beaches when they are empty and skip the group timetable entirely. The single best decision most Krabi visitors make; ask your advisor to time it to the tides for the sandbars and lagoons.

venues.name: Scuba diving the Andaman reefs
venues.note: Ao Nang is a full-service dive base for the local reefs and pinnacles around Phi Phi and the King Cruiser wreck, with leopard sharks, turtles and seasonal whale sharks and manta rays on the outer sites. Reputable centres run PADI courses and Discover Scuba dives, so a novice or a teenager can take a first breath underwater in warm, clear water.

venues.name: Snorkelling day trips
venues.note: For those who would rather stay on the surface, the shallow reefs off Bamboo, Chicken and the Phi Phi fringes deliver easy, colourful snorkelling straight off the boat. A private charter lets you reach the best patches at the quiet hours and keeps it gentle for children and non-swimmers with a guide.

venues.name: Ao Nang / Ao Thalane deep-water soloing & cliff jumping
venues.note: The purest thrill in Krabi: climbing unroped over the sea straight from a boat, then falling back into deep water when your grip gives, guided by the same climbing schools that run the Railay crags. For confident, adventurous travellers, an unforgettable half-day that only this coastline's overhanging karst makes possible.

venues.name: Nui Bay & the hidden southern coves of Lanta
venues.note: Beyond Kantiang, tiny bays like Nui and Bamboo tuck into the cliffs on the road to the national park, a string of near-private beaches for the traveller willing to drive to the island's wild southern end. The reward for renting a car on Lanta and chasing the emptiest sand in Krabi.

venues.name: The Grotto Bar
venues.note: Cocktails on the sand inside a limestone cave as the light goes over Phra Nang, the most singular sundowner in the region.
credentials: The bar of Rayavadee's cave restaurant (The Leading Hotels of the World), Krabi's signature setting for a sunset drink

venues.name: Rock Bar / beach bar, Phulay Bay
venues.area: Nong Thale (Phulay Bay, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve)
venues.note: An unhurried sundowner at Krabi's only Three-Key hotel, the most polished drink on the coast, on the water.
credentials: The signature bar of Phulay Bay, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, MICHELIN Three Keys (2025), Forbes Travel Guide

venues.name: REEVE Beach Club
venues.note: Ao Nang's prime beachfront club on the best corner of the bay, café by day, cocktails and a nightly fire show by the water after dark.
credentials: Ao Nang's established beachfront beach club, a recognised day-to-night venue on the main bay with a nightly fire show

venues.name: Rooftop bar, Ao Nang seafront
venues.note: The town's seafront rooftops catch the sunset over the islands, an easy elevated drink before dinner on the Ao Nang strip.
credentials: Ao Nang's seafront rooftop bars, the town's established sunset-drink circuit overlooking the bay and islands
